chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of our companions, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Among the people, there is one whose sustenance is in trade, and among them is one whose sustenance is in the sword, and among them is one whose sustenance is in his tongue.'

key_terms.السَّيْفِ: the sword (symbolizing military or political power)
key_terms.لِسَانِهِ: his tongue (symbolizing eloquence, speech, or scholarship)

ai.seo_question: What are the different types of sustenance (rizq) mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine distribution of rizq (provision), categorizing livelihood into trade, martial strength, and eloquence. This classification reflects the Shia understanding of varied societal roles as divinely ordained means of sustenance, highlighting how different talents serve distinct communal needs. The mention of 'speech' underscores the value of oratory and knowledge transmission in Islamic tradition.
